text:
Sofia Ivanova: seeing a streaming cadence regression on `fast` tier after the tier mapping landed. token cadence is “bursty” (clients get 4–8 tokens at once then stall). not just p95 overall, but per-token spacing. anyone else seeing this in perf-canary or staging?

Marcus Reed: yep. noticed in staging chat route. overall p95 isn’t terrible but `stream_token_gap_ms` spikes. looks like decode isn’t getting scheduled frequently enough when we’re aggressively trying to form batches.

Omar El-Sayed: +1. I can repro locally with the stream harness.

```
# repro (internal)
bench-lab run \
  --model rw-openchat-7b \
  --route chat_stream \
  --tier fast \
  --concurrency 32 \
  --prompt_bucket p50 \
  --duration 8m

# metric to watch
p95(stream_inter_token_ms)
```

Sofia Ivanova: what changed is we’re biasing prefill batching harder in fast tier than we intended. decode is waiting behind prefill to keep GPU busy, but streaming wants steady cadence even if it costs a bit.

Julian Moore: confirming from traces: long stretches where decode queue has ready work but scheduler keeps pulling prefill microbatches because `prefill_weight` dominates when `queue_depth_prefill > 0`.

Grace Kim: perf-canary run from last night flagged it but only on streaming workloads. non-streaming completions look fine.

Hiro Tanaka: proposal: add a “streaming decode urgency boost” so decode slices get scheduled more frequently. something like:
- if request has `stream=true` and `time_since_last_token_ms > X`, multiply decode priority
- cap prefill burst length while there are active streaming decodes

Sofia Ivanova: +1. I was thinking tweak in the tier mapping: for `fast` tier set `decode_priority_boost=1.4` and reduce `prefill_to_decode_ratio` a bit. also tighten `max_queue_delay_ms` for streaming only (not global) so we don’t accumulate as much burst.

Marcus Reed: the smallest code change might be in scheduler: when `streaming_active=true`, enforce a minimum decode service rate, e.g. after N prefill iterations we must run at least 1 decode iteration. avoids messing too much with model-specific weights.

Omar El-Sayed: careful: we added that “N” loop last quarter and it caused throughput drop on long-context. but if this is only gated on `streaming_active` + `fast` tier it should be ok.

Julian Moore: I can add a trace annotation to make this debuggable. e.g. span field `scheduler.reason=decode_urgency` vs `prefill_batching` so we can confirm what’s driving decisions.

Sofia Ivanova: what about tests? we need something deterministic enough to catch cadence regressions.

Rina Kobayashi: for perf-canary we can add a streaming cadence gate:
- `p95(inter_token_ms) <= 120ms` (numbers TBD by model)
- also monitor `p99` because the stalls show up there
We can start as “warn only” for a couple runs then flip to required.

Grace Kim: we already compute `first_token_latency_ms` and `tokens_per_second`. I can extend the report template with `inter_token_ms` histogram and a simple “burstiness score” (stddev of inter-token).

Marcus Reed: implementation plan:
1) scheduler tweak: when `tier=fast` and `streaming_active`, increase decode selection probability / enforce decode at least every K iterations
2) add unit/regression test in runtime scheduler tests simulating mixed prefill+decode queues and asserting decode isn’t starved
3) add perf-canary metric gates on streaming cadence

Sofia Ivanova: sounds good. please keep it scoped: only `fast` tier for now. standard/cost-efficient can accept more cadence variation.

Omar El-Sayed: I’ll take the scheduler change. will open PR today. (need a flag so we can revert fast.)

Julian Moore: I’ll add the trace fields + metric for `streaming_active` at scheduler tick. should help confirm in staging.

Hiro Tanaka: if we tweak weights, let’s do it in config mapping not hardcoded. but I’m ok with a minimal scheduler rule as stopgap.

Sofia Ivanova: ok, do the scheduler stopgap + config knob exposed so we can tune without another code change. something like `decode_urgency_boost`.

DeployBot: CI reminder: `runtime-perf-canary` failed on `chat_stream/fast` in `rw-openchat-7b` (run #11842). Link: https://github.com/redwood/perf-canary/actions/runs/11842

Grace Kim: that’s the one I saw. if we can get a patch in today, I’ll rerun canary on the branch.

Marcus Reed: Omar, when you open PR, can you include a quick before/after snippet from bench-lab? even just one run showing p95(inter_token) improvement.

Omar El-Sayed: will do.

Sofia Ivanova: also please add a note in the PR description: rationale is user-perceived streaming smoothness. we’ll accept a small throughput hit in `fast` tier if needed.

Rina Kobayashi: I’ll draft the perf-canary gate thresholds and put behind a config so we can calibrate per model family.

Julian Moore: fyi the regression is worse with tool-calls because prefill spikes (function schema) and then decode stalls. if your test can simulate “big prefill then small decode repeatedly” that’s the pattern.

Omar El-Sayed: good call. I can craft a scheduler test with:
- 2 large prefill jobs queued
- 20 streaming decode jobs trickling
- assert no decode gap > T ticks

Sofia Ivanova: perfect. let’s aim to merge by EOD so we don’t hold the beta ramp.

Marcus Reed: (reactions: :thumbsup: from Marcus Reed, :eyes: from Grace Kim)

Grace Kim: once merged I’ll rerun staging streaming smoke and post graphs.

Sofia Ivanova: thanks all. keep updates here.
